## Tangent Finance[​](#tangent-finance "Direct link to Tangent Finance")

Tangent is a [*Decentralized Finance*](https://www.investopedia.com/decentralized-finance-defi-5113835#:~:text=Decentralized%20finance%2C%20or%20DeFi%2C%20is,transact%20financially%20with%20each%20other.) (DeFi) protocol that provides highly capital-efficient synthetic stablecoin services.

Currently, Tangent features `USG`, an over-collateralized USD-denominated stablecoin, and its savings account version, `sUSG`.

Tangent functions as a [*Decentralized Autonomous Organization*](https://www.investopedia.com/tech/what-dao/) (DAO), and is governed by `TAN` token holders, who share most of the earnings generated by the platform and its products.

# Understanding USG

![Ban1](https://mintcdn.com/tangentfinance/K5ob5ysADobouXam/public/images/usg.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=K5ob5ysADobouXam\&q=85\&s=5bc305cd9a47bb7a73e1de2e64cb58e8)

## Overview[​](#overview "Direct link to Overview")

`USG` is an over-collateralized USD-denominated stablecoin that can be minted against a variety of productive collateral, such as [Curve Finance](https://www.curve.finance/dex/ethereum/pools/) LP tokens or [Pendle](https://www.pendle.finance/) PTs.

Under certain circumstances, `USG` can be borrowed interest-free on dedicated markets. When an interest rate is charged, the system uses a dynamic model that adjusts the interest rate depending on `USG`'s price.

As with other CDP protocols, a position on Tangent can be liquidated if its health ratio falls below a defined threshold, wherein the protocol considers that the position isn't sufficiently collateralized. Users are required to monitor their position to avoid liquidation.

`USG` can serve various needs and is particularly adapted to the following use cases:

* Leverage farming;
* Leverage trading;
* Low-risk yield farming on liquidity pools or the savings account.

## Markets[​](#markets "Direct link to Markets")

Tangent uses three different kinds of markets to mint `USG`, known as [*High Emissions Collateral*](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/hec_markets.md) (**HEC**), [*Low Emissions Collateral*](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/lec_markets.md) (**LEC**), and [*Fixed Interest Rate*](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/fir_markets.md) (**FIR**) markets.

On **HEC** markets, it is possible to borrow interest-free while `USG`'s price is above a predefined *price threshold*. Since the collateral used in these markets generates *liquid rewards* (such as `CRV`), the system deducts a portion of these rewards from borrowers as a form of payment. As `USG` goes down, the rewards cut goes up. If `USG` falls below the *price threshold*, 100% of rewards are cut, and a dynamic interest rate is charged while `USG` stays below this price.

On **LEC** markets, a dynamic and price-dependent interest rate is charged immediately. If the collateral generates liquid rewards, 97.5% of these rewards are streamed back to borrowers, as the protocol applies a 2.5% fee.

On both **HEC** and **LEC** markets, the interest rate goes up as `USG`'s price goes down.

On **FIR** markets, a fixed interest rate is charged immediately, independently of the price of `USG`. If the collateral generates liquid rewards, 90% of these rewards are streamed back to borrowers, as the protocol applies a 10% fee.

For more details, refer to the following sections:

> **[HEC markets](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/hec_markets.md)**

> **[LEC markets](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/lec_markets.md)**

> **[FIR markets](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/Markets/fir_markets.md)**

## Savings account[​](#savings-account "Direct link to Savings account")

`sUSG` is the savings version of `USG`, and stands for *staked Tangent USD*. It is a decentralized and unstoppable savings account that can be used in DeFi. To earn yield, it simply needs to be held in a wallet.

`sUSG` yield is fully endogenous, and comes from the system itself. It does not rely on governance token emissions.

For more details, refer to the following section:

> **[sUSG - Savings account](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/susg.md)**

## Stability[​](#stability "Direct link to Stability")

`USG` doesn't use redemptions and thus, can't be redeemed for its collateral. Instead, it protects its peg through a combinaison of Peg Keepers contracts, and a dynamic interest rate and rewards deduction model. This design has been proven efficient, and is inpired by [`crvUSD`](https://resources.curve.finance/crvusd/overview/).

As `USG`'s price deviates below \$1, the interest rate and the rewards deduction rate go up automatically. As a result, the more `USG` depegs downward, the more the system earns, and the stronger the incitation is for borrowers to repay their loans. Since most of the system's revenue are directed back towards liquidity pools and the savings account, `USG`'s attractiveness increases as its peg decreases.

For more details, refer to the following sections:

> **[Peg Keepers](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/peg_keepers.md)**

> **[Peg stability](https://docs.tangent.finance/docs/usg/peg-stability.md)**

## Self-sustainability[​](#self-sustainability "Direct link to Self-sustainability")

The system is designed so `USG` can grow and maintain its liquidity in a self-sustainable way, without relying on external incentives.

Many stablecoins depends on exogenous incentives, mostly to sustain their liquidity on DEXs. To do so, it is common to use governance tokens as a subsidy to incentivize users to provide liquidity. This is done either by directly rewarding liquidy providers with the governance token, or by issuing [*vote incentives*](https://pexx.com/chaindebrief/what-are-bribes-in-cryptocurrency-and-decentralized-finance/) on dedicated markets.

In contrast, `USG` uses most of its revenue to maintain its liquidity, and to provide a yield to its savings account, `sUSG`. Thus, the system doesn't rely on external incentives to be sustainable and grow, and can live indefinitely, without ever running out of incentives.

## Benefits of using USG[​](#benefits-of-using-usg "Direct link to Benefits of using USG")

As `USG` can be minted against a vast variety of productive collaterals, it is a versatile tool that can serve many purposes at once.

First and foremost, the stablecoin collaterals used by `USG` are generally more productive than those used in other CDP stablecoins. A high-yield collateral allows borrowers to sustain leverage farming strategies longer, and more efficiently.

On the other hand, when volatile collaterals are used in **HEC** market, `USG` can provide free leverage, whereas elsewhere, borrowers need to pay interest. In fact, when `USG` is above the market's *price threshold*, borrowers are paid to take leverage. On **LEC** markets, the rewards earned from collaterals can offset totally or partially the cost of borrowing. `USG` can then be, in many situations, the most capital-efficient way to open leveraged positions against volatile assets.

Finally, `USG` can be used for its yield opportunities on liquidity pools, or savings account.

Overall, given its design, `USG` is able to serve the needs of many market participants, from leveraged traders and farmers, to simple yield farmers, in a capital-efficient and secured way.

## Risks[​](#risks "Direct link to Risks")

> [!WARNING]
>
> * If your collateral is liquidated, you will not be able to recover it, but you will keep what you borrowed (if you are not using leverage). In the event of liquidation, there is no recourse possible. It is your responsability to manage your loan's health.
> * While thoroughly audited, `USG` and its infrastructure are currently undergoing beta testing. Due to its experimental status, investing in `USG` involves risk, and may result in a partial or total loss of your investment. It’s your responsibility to fully understand the risks associated with using `USG`.
> * The value of `USG` may fluctuate due to the market's volatility or sudden shifts in its liquidity.
> * `USG` is issued solely through smart contracts, without any intermediary. However, the parameters ensuring the proper functioning of the `USG` infrastructure may be updated based on decisions approved by the DAO. Users are expected to stay informed about any changes to the stablecoin infrastructure parameters.
